notes.notes: [h3]Taxi Simulator – Devlog: AI and Environment Systems[/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/a009ebf6591153ef59b69fa995b0e2168f039dce.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In recent weeks, we’ve mainly focused on developing our AI systems, improving NPC interactions, and further optimization.[/p][p][/p][p]The pedestrian system is now fully integrated with collision detection. Hitting a pedestrian results in a fine, and the pedestrian always gets back up—unless the player stops the car directly on them, in which case they get up only after the vehicle drives away. We’ve taken care of proper animations and environment reactions—after an incident, nearby NPCs respond appropriately and avoid the area for a while.[/p][p][/p][p]NPC AI is already working across most of the city. Pedestrians and vehicles can avoid each other and interact with simple objects (like phone booths). The system has been tested with 1,000 active NPCs near the player, consistently delivering around 50 FPS.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/5bcdd2d66f6af943e102b3bd95ec63a7b537d1e9.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We’ve added support for destructible objects—vehicles can ram into and deform them. Placing these objects on the map only requires specifying how they should react to collisions.[/p][p][/p][p]The weather system is now dynamic, and atmospheric conditions affect the environment (for example, puddles during rain or water drops on car bodies). Plant movement in response to wind is either in the works or partially implemented.[/p][p][/p][p]Traffic systems are still being developed—so far, we’ve mostly improved vehicle-player collisions. Work in this area is ongoing.[/p][p][/p][p]Apart from that, we’ve improved various mechanics and carried out more optimization. One known issue involves physics: in rare cases, a car can flip over if an NPC lands on the hood. This is related to changes introduced in Unreal Engine 5.5.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/e6a8e7ac814cfc3c745ec690ec03a6e0b56d2bb8.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We tested various approaches to procedural map generation (PCG)—the current system is stable, pending final approval. We also reworked the lake environment (ultimately moving away from Nanite assets).[/p][p][/p][p]We’ve introduced a new standard for road width and lane count, along with tools for faster road editing. Our detail generation tools (like custom walls) have been improved, buildings have been updated (packed level actor), and new elements have been added to the demo area.[/p][p][/p][p]The phone UI has been updated: new graphics, backgrounds, and refreshed designs for the mechanic and taxi apps. An initial version of the HUD with minimap and notifications is also in place.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s it for the major updates. More soon.[/p][p][/p][p]Regarding our YouTube devlogs, the upcoming ones will most likely be in Polish with subtitles. Posting videos in alternating languages creates some confusion for new viewers.[/p]

notes.title: Even GTA VI Had a First Day — How We’re Building Taxi Simulator
notes.notes:

We’re doing something new. For the first time, instead of writing a traditional devlog, we decided to prepare a short video too. Yeah, I’m aware my commentary is still pretty rookie-level — give me a few episodes to warm up.

Laying the foundation for a playable demo, including quest logic.

Fuel management without the frustration — dynamic delivery based on your location.

AI cars that drive, turn, and stop like semi-decent humans.

📍 Watch the full devlog on YouTube

https://youtu.be/r9o26Sz2e_I

notes.title: Whole Lotta Yellow
notes.notes:
Yello.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/ec0b85b892433027c15e8e954bf5bd4015fcb350.png[/img]

We had an unusually hands-on March, which mostly went into improving the existing content, but a few new things were added, too.

The biggest ones are:

1. Traffic System. Standard feature for this kind of game; no need to elaborate. There are roads, AI cars drive on them. A classic, standard feature, but we've implemented it, so we're letting you know.

2. Game Structure. The loop roughly looks like this:

cutscene (a few dozen seconds) - mission (a few minutes) - grind (a few minutes) - cutscene (a few dozen seconds)

Of course, the time spent on missions or grinding will depend on your skills and preferences. I recommend imagining the flow of Taxi Simulator as something similar to what’s known from Underground 2. So, we have an open world with missions to trigger (which can be repeated in case of failure), and in between missions, we can do taxi orders to earn money, upgrade the car, and approach missions with a better handicap.

Right now, we're focusing on skills and phone handling. We’ll probably finish these features in April.

notes.title: Swing down, sweet chariot, stop and let me ride
notes.notes:
We’re alive, unfortunately. Gotta keep going.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/c08fca35dcb3ec4a4a862a2c32c7e182a83e73ef.png[/img]

The biggest addition this time is the tuning system. Technically, we took inspiration from the best racing series ever—Need for Speed Underground. The system will keep evolving because we’re watching every season of Pimp My Ride. For now, you can tweak the basics—engine, suspension, tires, etc. We also added a bunch of visual customization options.

The driving model got another round of improvements. Still looking at NFS, but also at Forza. It won’t be that good, because we’re not in that league, but it’s pretty solid.

We added a save system. Now you can safely turn off your computer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/5862acf503d9e15acdac64e38bdee32716e1c1bc.png[/img]

The Journal is in—stats, story progress, everything in one place. It’s clear and easy to check where you stand.

We made our own taxi model. Until now, we were driving some junk from the marketplace. Now, we have our own junk.

There’s also a maintenance system. It’s not Car Mechanic Simulator, but the taxi can get damaged and dirty, so we added repair and cleaning options. If you crash too much or someone throws up on the upholstery, you can fix it up and get back on the road.

And of course, we’re constantly working on expanding the city and its surroundings.

notes.title: Outskirts
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/9cad2b1666cc05cd2077c65ad21733891b6f6652.jpg[/img]

Basically, we’re writing to let you know we’re still alive.

We’re bouncing back after the first delay. While the city is steadily improving—blockouts replaced with shiny placeholders—the countryside has been razed to the ground twice already. The original concept looked great on paper, but practice said otherwise. This is our third attempt, with the same hope but a lot more experience.

For now, we’re focusing on the bare basics—terrain, minimal vegetation (driving on blockout concrete is a nightmare), and roads. Obviously, road design is key, so we’re holding off on further stages until testing proves the level design delivers fun. Buildings will come last since they’re time-consuming to make and don’t impact gameplay much. Aesthetic polish is the cherry on top we’re saving for later.

On the bright side, features are progressing as planned. In the next devlog, we’ll sum up how the feature work is coming along.

notes.title: December 2024
notes.notes:
Greetings, comrades.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/35280558/9760652e58f128f59776eef46c2b84e66f99236b.jpg[/img]

As the year draws to a close, here’s a quick rundown. Before you tune out, let me present the agenda—maybe one of the topics will catch your interest, and you can jump straight to it:

1. **Priest Simulator**  
2. **Mercyful Flames**  
3. **Taxi Simulator**  
4. **Your Principal**  

[h1]Priest Simulator[/h1]

Our most recognized franchise so far is keeping us busy:

The **Vampire Show** has left Early Access. However, we’ve already received feedback about some messed-up lipsync and issues with the final raid not registering correctly. We’ve fixed the first problem, and we’re working on the second. A patch is on its way.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2947900/Priest_Simulator_Her_Ghost_DLC/

We’ve released *Her Ghost*, a DLC for *Vampire Show*, offering about an hour of new gameplay. Some of you may remember that we declared the game finished months ago, but for various reasons, the launch was delayed. Sure, any game can be endlessly improved, so we added a few more cards to the Trello board. Plus, we wanted to experiment with creating DLC, so we decided to add new content roughly on the scale of *Heavy Duty*. Big thanks to everyone who purchased it.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/35280558/a600c086e2e6a9d8b55b48b80c2334850957a4b6.jpg[/img]

We also made the soundtrack available some time ago. You can listen to it on Spotify or YouTube. The music video for the standout track *Legion* is doing pretty well at festivals:

- Winner: Best Polish Animated Music Video at PL Music Video Awards 2024  
- Winner: *Black Horse of Music Videos* at Ars Independent 2024  
- Semi-finalist: Azyl Shorts 2024  

It was also officially selected for:  
Animakom Fest 2024,  
Żubroffka 2024 (Music Video category),  
Animest 2024,  
Splat!FilmFest 2024,  
Grand Video Awards 2024 (Music Video category),  
Offeliada 2024,  
Linoleum 2024.  

Watch it here:  
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oMop-7BM4ds  

That’s not all the news from the *Priest* universe. We’ve been working for months on the next installment, *Wolf Moon*. It continues threads from the previous games but takes them in a very different direction. It’s a low-poly action RPG inspired by MOBAs and *Vampire Survivors*. We intended to release the Steam page this year, but it’s not yet up to our standards.

[h1]Mercyful Flames[/h1]

We’ve really gone all out on this one. Last year, we made the tough decision to rework the game completely—a decision that was challenging but ultimately necessary. The original concept of a card-based RPG might resurface in a future project, but not here. *Mercyful Flames* always had great atmosphere but struggled with the transition of our physical designs into a digital format. 

This time, we went all in, inspired by a friend’s comment: “I’d buy a *Priest* game that’s just cutscenes.” While it’s an oversimplification, it nudged us toward creating a minimalist, gameplay-light experience.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/35280558/9f43649f9c317bbbe19503dc7c6f5949339f975b.jpg[/img]

The game is going through what feels like its hundredth iteration. I admit I’ve gone a bit obsessive, tweaking every little detail. We keep adding minor dialogues or effects to enhance the illusion of a living world. The game is divided into dozens of “scenes,” and polishing one often makes others look subpar in comparison. At that point, we have to even things out, one way or another.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1066740/Mercyful_Flames_The_Witches/

As with *Vulgator*, we’ve collaborated with acclaimed Polish artists. This time, we worked with *Alembik*, a duo comprising Robert and Michał. You might know Michał from *Owls Woods Graves*, *Over the Voids*, and *Mgła* (live). They composed the soundtrack, which will also be available as a standalone album on streaming platforms.

[h1]Taxi Simulator[/h1]

Now for our biggest project. We’ve been dedicating our lives to this one and regularly post devlogs about its progress. The game has a completely different vibe from anything we’ve done before—less experimental, more craftsmanship. This time, the title isn’t some ironic twist; it’s exactly what it says.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1159390/Taxi_Simulator/

**Your Principal** is temporarily on hold by mutual agreement with the publisher. We’ll return to it next year.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1176330/Your_Principal/

Apart from these titles, we’re also working on a port—or rather, a remaster—of a certain hit, but we’re not revealing any details yet.

By the way, you might have read rumors that we’re quitting game development to start selling weapons. Some reliable Polish media outlets got their facts and companies mixed up. I won’t bother denying it because it works in our favor.

notes.title: m.A.A.p of the City
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/60bc8e8a24d0fe06fc1be0bb7bba2e68db3ed0b7.png[/img]

Since the last time we shared a devlog with you, the project has consumed hundreds of work hours. We've managed to create a pretty solid driving model and the core systems needed to build the heart of the game—delivering customers. We've already implemented essential features like a clock, bank account, job management, GPS, penalties and rewards, and a client generator.

We've also designed the city map. The area is fictional, though it serves as a tribute to one of our favorite games. We won’t reveal the title just yet—maybe some of you can guess the reference. For now, the terrain is flat, but milestone by milestone, we’ll add unique landmarks and terrain details inspired by real-world locations, primarily in the U.S.

In Taxi Simulator, you’ll also be able to venture beyond the city limits. Rural areas are part of the plan. Right now, the entire map is a single monolithic space, but we’ll eventually divide it into districts that you’ll unlock as you earn the proper permits. If needed, we’ll expand the map, but for now, it’s big enough to support the scale we’re aiming for.

If you have favorite or iconic locations you'd love to see, let us know in the comments. We’re Polish developers, and honestly, most of our knowledge about the U.S. comes from movies. If there’s a spot that gets requested repeatedly or a particular view that really inspires us, we’ll make sure to include it in the game.

notes.title: Your Expectations
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/d048268eb120b7e0d968e2cc0f83b93e0554e9a9.png[/img]

Guys, at some point, there will probably be a Q&A cycle where we report on what we broke, what we removed, what worked, and what still might work. But today’s plan is a little different. Since the game is in its early stages, we can still take the time to consider. Consider what might go sideways and what we should be thinking through. Let's call this the first phase of the project—the first of three. This is the phase where we can still design and test solutions. Once we enter the second phase, the core decisions from the first phase will generally be locked in and won't be up for changes.

To put it plainly: now’s the best time to throw in your feedback, because with each day, the chance to act on it gets slimmer. We’ve got a table tracking all your suggestions, and we’re taking every little note into account. Huge thanks for the solid batch of feedback you left under the last [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1159390/eventcomments/4845401032851248400?snr=2_9_100000_&ctp=2]devlog[/url]—keep it coming.

You know how it is: sometimes your suggestions take the game in totally different directions. In the end, the call is up to Asmodev, but it’s always better to do some proper research. And there’s no better research than what’s in your comments here. Lol, getting a bit sentimental, but screw it. Say whatever you want; we’ll keep making the game.

Have a dreadful Halloween.

To address the production issues and ensure the delivery of a superior gaming experience, the development team made the critical decision to transition to Unreal Engine 5. This engine change required significant effort, but we firmly believe it will pave the way for the game's success and seamless performance.

💡 New Team, New Ideas 💡

With the engine switch came a brand-new team, brimming with fresh ideas and passion for Taxi Simulator. These folks revved up their creativity and worked tirelessly to bring you an exhilarating experience.

We have already presented Manhattan several times, which looked like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/d1b54444ea241f42b81a15f2e399344eda56ab59.png[/img]

And like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/705c4e2ff6cecf95f6aa2401e44798279101f05a.png[/img]

These are still the same streets, but their magic is determined by the lighting. It makes the game look more realistic, we enjoy not only completing missions, but also driving aimlessly...

Although it's a detail, it is - in our opinion - especially important in open-world games. The very performance of the mission is one thing, but we want players to come back to the game also when they just want to ride and relax 😉

[h2]What does lighting work mean?[/h2]

[b]- Color temperature [/b]- we set it to make the light effect spatial. It is thanks to this that the sun between the leaves seems real
[b]- Light propagation [/b]- how far is it to go, where and what it will affect, and where and how strongly it is reflected from individual buildings.

We are also working on the post process - these are various effects, including color tweaking, but also vignettes, photo effects. It's also about working on presets for different times of the day and different weather conditions, so that a foggy morning or a rainy evening is as real as possible.

Here is a small video from our invaluable partner Beffio how Manhattan looks by day and by night:

[previewyoutube=gVPtADw4sss;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Taxi Simulator: DevLog #8
notes.notes:
[b]Hey, Taxi Drivers![/b]

We're arriving with a new devlog! Lately there was a lot of showcasing of our progress regarding the game's graphical side - you could witness our interpetation of the look and the feel of New York City, as it will be portrayed in Taxi Simulator :D

Today we've decided to try something different and tell you about... our [b]inspirations[/b]. Popculture inspirations 😉 Sometimes the best ideas for games come from watching some good old TV during the evening…

Let's start with something not obviously associated with driving a taxi. Do you remember The [i]A-Team[/i]? Yes, we're aware that instead of a yellow taxi, a black B.A. Van comes to mind 😉 But hear us out... There was this one episode, during which our brave crew of veterans helped a taxi company fight of a corporation wanting to take over all cab routes. We're wondering how we could include this idea in our script 😉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/f36c93c75a34f00bdc38d12e930fb6efa01257cf.jpg[/img]

Time for a more obvious inspiration - [i]Taxi Driver[/i] and the extraordinary role of Robert De Niro. If, while adding our game to your wishlist, you were wondering whether this movie will be one of our inspirations, then yes - it most definitely [u][b]IS[/b][/u] :D We couldn't afford to ignore a masterpiece of this magnitude while making a game about driving a taxi. Besides, we bet that anyone hailing a taxi hopes that Robert De Niro will be sitting behind the wheel 😉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/45a2e61b57088df90e007a6cf20964ad3e9261b9.jpg[/img]

To wrap this up we would like to finish with an inspiration from our own backyard - [i]Zmiennicy[/i] ("Subs"). Not well known outside of Poland, but in our country it was a huge hit! Of course in old times 😉 To quickly summarize the plot - the main hero Jacek had a cab, but lacked a sub. At the same time Kasia was looking for a job as a taxi driver, but couldn't be hired on account of being a woman (SEXISM - unthinkable by today's standards!). But she didn't give up and decided to dress as a man, ultimately landing a job as Jacek's sub. Sounds like a soap opera? :D Yup, a little bit. [u][b]SPOILER ALERT:[/b][/u] they fell in love and lived happily ever after 😉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35845552/8031c5b679b95654d046d79f3be4cca04223d6da.jpg[/img]

We could go on forever writing about our inspirations, but we're curious if you could recommend a movie or a tv series which would be a NEW inspiration. If that is the case, then don't hesitate to let us know in the comment section - we will look through all the comments! 😉 


PS. GTA is also our inspiration. If we didn't include it, than we wouldn't be making a game about cars 😉


Cheers,
Taxi Drivers from Woodland Games.
